edges.effect_quant: The most current pooled evidence suggests that more digital-screen time is associated with higher odds of myopia, with risk rising as daily exposure climbs.
edges.mechanism: High screen exposure combines prolonged near work, reduced blink rate, short viewing distances, and often less outdoor time, all of which plausibly push refractive development toward myopia. The exact causal contribution of screens versus the broader educational and indoor-life package remains uncertain, but the aggregate signal now leans harmful.
edges.summary: The best current summary is that heavy screen time is probably a myopia risk factor, even if it is not the only one and not the strongest one. Newer dose-response meta-analyses find higher odds of myopia with greater daily screen exposure, while older reviews were more equivocal because the literature was thinner and more heterogeneous.
edges.caveats: A large part of this literature is observational, so screen time is tangled with education, near-work intensity, and less time outdoors. This edge should be read as a modifiable risk signal rather than proof that screens alone drive the myopia epidemic.
